bug_semantics: An unauthenticated POST to the WebUI /ui/login endpoint reaches userpass_auth(). For a nonexistent username, select_account_name() yields no ui_account and the handler immediately renders a response saying that no account is associated with that identity. For an existing username paired with a wrong password, execution instead attempts get_auth_token_user_pass() and renders a different cannot-get-auth-token response. Comparing those response bodies therefore reveals whether the supplied username exists (CWE-204); analogous distinct account/token failure responses were also present in the SAML paths.
flaw_origin: The smallest source commit is PR #4082 member 0f88777af4716552155edfd99731eff2571d4f7b, which created the Flask WebUI implementation, including main.py's POST /login dispatch to userpass_auth() and common/utils.py's distinct no-account and bad-token responses. GitHub later squash-landed the eight-member PR as d8f7c9e943500f0ef0fc705a200d50f436d22605 on the main lineage and e0dd5a9b9393c74fc7395d4e4970f2c31ee08ad4 on the 1.23 maintenance lineage; those squash commits are landing artifacts, not the true BIC.
ai_marker: BIC commit object 0f88777af4716552155edfd99731eff2571d4f7b has human author and committer Thomas Beermann <thomas.beermann@cern.ch> and the complete message 'Webui: add flask implementation #4041'. It contains no Co-authored-by, Generated-with, AI attribution trailer, bot identity, or other AI marker.
evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/rucio/rucio/security/advisories/GHSA-38wq-6q2w-hcf9 gives the /ui/login POC: nonexistent identity 15251087 returns 'Cannot get find any account associated with 15251087 identity.', while existing root with a wrong password returns 'Cannot get auth token. It is possible that the presented identity root is not mapped to any Rucio account root.'; the bundle records patched boundaries 35.8.3, 38.5.4, and 39.3.1. In the validated clone, `git log --all -S'Cannot get find any account associated with' -- lib/rucio/web/ui/flask/common/utils.py` finds squash landings d8f7c9e943500f0ef0fc705a200d50f436d22605 and e0dd5a9b9393c74fc7395d4e4970f2c31ee08ad4. GitHub's first-party `GET /repos/rucio/rucio/pulls/4082/commits` enumerates the eight member SHAs recorded above; rerunning `git log --reverse -S'Cannot get find any account associated with' f49c5c9599e147823110dc6da22a0bc33a881f8e..b0049b7c7d08258389cf8bd4bcdf21ca830c54e7 -- lib/rucio/web/ui/flask/common/utils.py` returns only 0f88777af4716552155edfd99731eff2571d4f7b. `git log -L ':userpass_auth:lib/rucio/web/ui/flask/common/utils.py' 0f88777af4716552155edfd99731eff2571d4f7b` likewise attributes the whole newly added vulnerable function to 0f88777. `git diff --name-status f49c5c9599e147823110dc6da22a0bc33a881f8e 0f88777af4716552155edfd99731eff2571d4f7b -- lib/rucio/web/ui/flask/common/utils.py` reports A, and `git cat-file -e f49c5c9599e147823110dc6da22a0bc33a881f8e:lib/rucio/web/ui/flask/common/utils.py` fails because the path does not exist, directly proving parent absence. `git diff --name-status 1.23.10 1.23.11 -- .../utils.py` reports A via maintenance squash e0dd5a9, while `git tag --contains d8f7c9e943500f0ef0fc705a200d50f436d22605` begins on the main release line at 1.24.0rc1/1.24.0. Direct main-line fix 0b22b350201bcf040aa1aade476cf69944019d97 changes userpass_auth() and both SAML flows to initialize token to None, attempt token creation only when ui_account exists, and return the same generic authentication-failed response for either missing-account or token failure. Its equivalent backports are 33bc01dc055c8e52a688404068419c916fab797f, 949ff8cfd7efb51c71cdceb5e80be8f6858e0b73, and 1ea6771b43c7ae45485486692189e40fbe61f496; `git for-each-ref --contains=<sha> --format='%(refname)' refs/tags` shows their first containing tags as 35.8.3, 38.5.4, and 39.3.1 respectively, while the immediately preceding 35.8.2, 38.5.3, and 39.3.0 tags do not contain them. `git diff 35.8.2 35.8.3 -- lib/rucio/web/ui/flask/common/utils.py` directly displays the distinct-message-to-generic-message boundary. Finally, `git cat-file -p 0f88777af4716552155edfd99731eff2571d4f7b` reproduces the human identities and one-line message quoted in ai_marker, with no trailers.
reasoning: The vulnerability is the response discrepancy itself, not a later refactor: the first PR member created both the public login dispatch and the two observably different failure branches. Because the public landing commits aggregate eight reconstructable PR members, selecting either squash would violate the smallest-BIC rule; decomposition isolates 0f88777, and its direct parent lacks the entire Flask utility file. The direct fix and its release-branch equivalents collapse the relevant branches to a generic failure, matching the advisory and patched-tag boundaries. AI classification is restricted to the true BIC commit object; that object attributes the change solely to a human and has no canonical AI signal, so the supported closed verdict is NOT_AI.
